Common questions

For anything else, ask an engineer.

Do you sell individual LED modules or complete screens?

Both. Our core business is manufacturing LED display modules, which we supply to OEMs, integrators and installers. We also supply complete display configurations for commercial and project customers. Tell us what you need and we’ll confirm the scope in writing.

Which pixel pitch should I choose?

Start from the closest viewing distance. As a rule of thumb, the closest comfortable distance in metres is roughly the pitch in millimetres: P2.5 from about 3 m, P4 from 4 m, P4.81 from about 5 m and P10 from 10 m. The pitch guide goes into more detail.

Which modules are rated for outdoor use?

The P4.81 and P10 are IP65-rated for outdoor installations. The P4 has outdoor-level brightness with a published IP41 rating, so fully exposed sites need a protective cabinet. The P2.5 is an indoor module.

Can I get a sample before a bulk order?

Yes. We send samples for compatibility and quality checks, particularly to OEM and integrator customers planning repeat orders.

How is content updated on the display?

Our displays use synchronous control and work out of the box. Content can be changed through a cloud system from a phone or laptop, over 3G, 4G, 5G or a wired connection.

Where are you based?

Our corporate office is in ECIL and our factory is in the Cherlapally Industrial Development Area, both in Hyderabad, India.

About the P2.5 module

The GKAI P2.5 module is built for indoor video walls that need detailed, full-colour images at short viewing distances. Its SMD1515 three-in-one LEDs from Everlight are placed by SMT lines, which keeps colour even across the wall.

Refresh runs at 2,880 Hz as standard and supports up to 3,840 Hz, so the wall stays free of flicker and scan lines on camera. That matters in boardrooms, studios and anywhere the screen is filmed or photographed.

The 320 × 160 mm format fits the most common cabinet sizes, which makes the P2.5 a straightforward choice for integrators building or servicing indoor walls.

About the P10 module

The P10 is the long-distance module in the GKAI range. Its 10 mm pitch and SMD2727 LEDs are designed for audiences 10 to 100 metres away, where a finer pitch adds cost without adding visible detail.

At 115 W/m² average and 340 W/m² maximum, it has the lowest power draw of our modules, which keeps running costs down on large boards that stay lit for long hours.

IP65 protection and a −20 °C to 60 °C working range suit roadside, rooftop and facade installations. The 55° vertical viewing angle is tuned for screens mounted above eye level.

Its rated 2,500 cd/m² brightness suits long-distance boards, shaded or north-facing sites and screens that run mainly from dusk. For screens facing direct midday sun, ask us about higher-brightness configurations, or consider the P4.81 at 5,500–6,000 cd/m².

Recommended applications

  • Building facades and rooftop signage
  • Outdoor scrolling message boards

Pixel pitch guide: P2.5, P4, P4.81 and P10

How to choose pixel pitch, brightness and protection for an LED display, using real figures from our modules.

8 m
P2.53–30 m P44–15 m P4.814.8–48 m P1010–100 m

What pixel pitch means

Pixel pitch is the distance in millimetres from the centre of one pixel to the centre of the next. A P2.5 module has pixels 2.5 mm apart; a P10 has them 10 mm apart. A smaller pitch puts more pixels in the same area: our P2.5 has 160,000 dots per square metre, the P10 has 10,000.

Finer pitch costs more and draws more power, so choose the coarsest pitch that still looks solid from where your audience stands.

Matching pitch to viewing distance

A common rule of thumb: the closest comfortable viewing distance in metres is roughly the pitch in millimetres. Any closer and people start to see individual dots.

  • P2.5: 3 to 30 m. Boardrooms, lobbies, retail walls.
  • P4: 4 to 15 m. Bright interiors and transit.
  • P4.81: 4.8 to 48 m. Stages, events, outdoor walls.
  • P10: 10 to 100 m. Roadside boards and facades.

Indoor and outdoor modules compared

Brightness

Brightness is measured in candela per square metre (cd/m², often called nits). Indoor screens need around 600–1,000 cd/m²; much more is uncomfortable to look at. Screens in daylight need several thousand. Our P4 and P4.81 deliver 5,000–6,000 cd/m².

Ingress protection

The IP rating describes resistance to dust and water. IP65 is dust-tight and protected against water jets, which exposed outdoor sites need. IP41 suits indoor and sheltered locations.

Temperature

Outdoor modules need a wider working range. Our P10 is rated from −20 °C to 60 °C and the P4.81 from −10 °C to 60 °C.

Module, cabinet or complete display

A module is the smallest unit: a PCB with LEDs and drivers, such as our 320 × 160 mm P2.5. A cabinet is a frame holding several modules with power supplies and a receiving card. A complete display adds the controller, content software, structure and installation. Be clear which of these you are buying, and which your supplier is responsible for.

Procurement checklist

Before approving an LED display specification, make sure you have an answer for each line.

  • Pixel pitch and viewing distance
  • Brightness in cd/m²
  • IP rating, front and rear
  • Module dimensions and resolution

  • Scan rate
  • Refresh rate
  • Average and peak power

About GKAI Display Systems

We design and manufacture LED display modules in Hyderabad, India, for screen builders, integrators and project teams.

GKAI Display Systems Pvt Ltd was established in 2024. Our factory in Hyderabad, India, designs and manufactures LED modules on automated production lines.

The business is run by signage professionals with more than 25 years in the industry. Each requirement gets individual attention, from concept and design to finished modules.
